draft.exec:
Straits Commerce Bank needs an internal agent platform where staff can run AI agents safely over bank documents, while keeping all data in Singapore.

This proposal places the entire platform inside a private network in Singapore. It isolates agent code execution, serves a post-trained model for document search, and logs every action.

The result is a governed environment where staff use AI without exposing internal data. To move forward, confirm which open model you plan to post-train so the team can size the compute.

needs.need: Search over internal documents using RAG.
needs.answer: A dedicated service retrieves answers from your documents using a tuned model. Staff get accurate responses grounded in bank knowledge rather than public internet data.

needs.need: Post-training of an open model on bank data.
needs.answer: Managed training jobs fine-tune the model on your documents without running permanent clusters. Compute scales down when training finishes, reducing idle spend.
Agents run in isolated environments that keep generated code away from the rest of the bank network. This lowers the risk of accidental or malicious actions during internal workflows.

outcomes.title: Isolated agent execution
outcomes.text: Each agent runs in its own sandbox, separated from other workloads. This limits the blast radius if generated code behaves unexpectedly during internal tasks.

outcomes.title: Variable training costs
outcomes.text: Post-training uses managed GPU jobs that run only when needed. You avoid paying for idle training infrastructure between tuning cycles.

outcomes.title: Governed model access
outcomes.text: A central gateway enforces token limits and guardrails on every model call. This prevents runaway usage and keeps internal queries within policy.

outcomes.title: Centralized activity log
outcomes.text: Agent actions, model calls and training jobs write to a single log store. This gives your teams one place to review platform activity.

why.ack: Your team needs a foundation to host the agent platform, gateways and services across two zones in Singapore. A managed Kubernetes cluster reduces the operational effort of running this infrastructure yourselves.
why.acs-agent-sandbox: You asked for sandboxed code execution for agents. VM-isolated pods with warm pools let agents run generated code safely, lowering the risk to internal systems without slowing down staff.
why.ai-gateway: Multiple agents and services will call your models. Central routing with token limits and guardrails controls spend and reduces the chance of misuse across the bank.
why.elasticsearch: You need retrieval-augmented generation over internal documents. A managed vector store handles hybrid search for your RAG workflows, saving the team from operating search infrastructure themselves.
why.nat: Base models must be downloaded from the internet while data stays in Singapore. Controlled outbound access lets training jobs fetch weights without opening inbound paths to your private network.
why.oss: Internal documents, training datasets and model weights need durable storage within Singapore. Object storage holds these assets at low cost and feeds them directly into training and retrieval jobs.
why.agentcore: You are building an internal agent platform for bank workflows. An enterprise orchestration layer governs how agents use skills and tools, reducing the effort to manage them manually.
why.pai-eas: You requested RAG over internal documents and post-training of an open model. Managed serving hosts both the tuned model and the retrieval service behind private endpoints, scaling with demand.
why.pai-dlc: You asked for post-training of an open model. Managed training jobs provide GPUs only when fine-tuning runs, avoiding the fixed cost of permanent training clusters.
why.acr: Agent sandboxes and services require private container images. A managed registry with scanning stores these images securely, reducing the effort of maintaining your own image pipeline.
why.sls: Banks typically need to trace internal platform activity. Centralized logging captures agent actions and model calls, giving compliance teams searchable records without building a log system from scratch.

tradeoffs.text: The design assumes your team can operate Kubernetes. If not, managing the cluster adds operational burden.
tradeoffs.mitigation: Evaluate whether your team has this skill, or discuss a serverless container alternative with the account team.

tradeoffs.text: The platform assumes internal bank staff only, with no public exposure.
tradeoffs.mitigation: Confirm whether partners will ever access the agents; if so, the gateway configuration needs adjustment.

tradeoffs.text: Training jobs fetch base models through outbound internet access.
tradeoffs.mitigation: NAT Gateway restricts this to outbound traffic only, and all internal data remains in Singapore.

next: Schedule a cost-estimate session with the account team once the model and ingestion method are chosen.
Confirm which open model you plan to post-train so the team can size the compute for training and serving.
Decide how internal documents will be ingested into the vector store, such as batch upload or real-time sync.
